metadata.physics_model: physics3d v1 (Earth point + J2, Chebyshev DE440 Moon, Sun tidal, SRP)
metadata.validation: Matches JPL Horizons within 0.02 km RMS / 0.34 km max (Phase D gate: 1 km RMS / 10 km max)
metadata.source: NASA JPL Horizons API + NASA mission update blogs (April 2026)

events.name: Liftoff
events.description: SLS Block 1 lifted off from Kennedy Space Center LC-39B with the Artemis II crew on board.

events.name: Core stage / ICPS sep
events.description: SLS core stage separated; ICPS coast began.

events.name: ICPS perigee raise
events.description: ICPS performed the perigee raise burn to circularize Orion into a high Earth orbit (HEO) suitable for trans-lunar departure.

events.name: Orion / ICPS sep
events.description: Orion separated from the ICPS upper stage and began its independent flight.

events.name: Tracking begins
events.description: JPL Horizons tracking begins for Orion at this epoch (~3.5 hours post-launch). All physics simulation starts here.

events.name: TLI
events.description: ESM AJ10 main engine burn at HEO perigee. Source: NASA blog Apr 2 + energy method on Horizons.

events.name: OTC-1 (cancelled)
events.description: First outbound trajectory correction was cancelled — the trajectory was nominal and required no adjustment.

events.name: OTC-2 (cancelled)
events.description: Second outbound trajectory correction was also cancelled.

events.name: OTC-3
events.description: Only OTC that fired (OTC-1 and OTC-2 cancelled). Source: NASA blog Apr 5 + Horizons.

events.name: Lunar perilune
events.description: Closest approach to the Moon — 6,546 km above the lunar surface (8,283 km from Moon center). Free-return slingshot complete.

events.name: RTC-1
events.description: First return correction. Source: NASA blog Apr 7 (FD7 8:03 PM EDT).

events.name: RTC-2
events.description: Second return correction. Source: NASA blog Apr 9 (FD9 10:53 PM EDT).

events.name: RTC-3
events.description: Final entry alignment burn. Source: NASA blog Apr 10 (FD10 2:53 PM EDT).

events.name: Atmospheric entry interface
events.description: Orion crossed the atmospheric entry interface at ~120 km altitude, beginning hypersonic re-entry.

events.name: Splashdown (simulated)
events.description: Mission Tracker simulator prediction. Differs from published splashdown by ~800 km because Orion's precise bank-modulation schedule (which controls effective L/D during entry) is not publicly available. The simulator uses an empirical L/D = 0.05 average that produces a Pacific landing in the right region.

events.name: Splashdown (published)
events.description: Published Artemis II splashdown — Pacific Ocean ~50 miles off the coast of San Diego, California. Recovery by USS John P. Murtha.
